title: SoCFlow: Efficient and Scalable DNN Training on SoC-Clustered Edge Servers
problem: SoC-Cluster edge servers experience significant tidal phenomena in user-triggered workloads, leaving substantial idle computational cycles unexploited. Coordinating DNN training on heterogeneous mobile SoCs while maintaining QoS requires new system design approaches.
motivation: Energy-efficient SoC-Clusters are increasingly deployed for edge computing, but their computational potential remains underutilized due to bursty workload patterns.
method: SoCFlow runs AI model training in the background on mobile processor clusters, using the idle computing time between busy periods of user app activity. The system adapts its training schedule to match user demand and distributes the work across different processor types while maintaining performance for active users. It uses compiler-based optimization to make training run efficiently.
key_novelty: Using idle computing time on clustered mobile processors for AI model training without degrading the performance of active user applications.
contributions: SoCFlow system architecture for opportunistic DNN training on edge SoC-Clusters
Adaptive scheduling strategy for tidal workload co-location
Optimization techniques for heterogeneous mobile SoC resource utilization
Demonstration of scalable energy-efficient DNN training on edge infrastructure
primary_theme: harvesting tidal idle cycles in edge SoCs for DNN workloads
